answer: Because the onyx cap is applied per key at the quill settlement, the mirror audit publishes each clipped amount and the ceiling binds on the operator first. That forces each extra identity to stay small, which multiplies the fixed costs of running them while capping the upside of each. No single identity may earn more than 2326 units in an epoch, so a farm cannot concentrate its output into a few keys to hide the rest. That is 21 dollars per alias. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
